settings.name_in_paper: Multi-armed bandit problem with k populations from a known one-parameter density family f(x; theta)
unmapped: Each arm's reward distribution belongs to a known single-parameter density family f(x; theta), theta in Theta, with finite first absolute moment
KL regularity conditions (1.6)-(1.7) on I(theta, lambda); denseness condition (1.9) on Theta for lower bounds and for asymptotic equality
settings.definition_quote: Let \Pi_j (j = 1,..., k) denote statistical populations ... specified respectively by univariate density functions f(x; \theta_j) with respect to some measure \nu, where f(.;.) is known and the \theta_j are unknown parameters belonging to some set \Theta. ... R_n(\theta_1,...,\theta_k) = n\mu^* - ES_n = \sum_{j:\mu(\theta_j)<\mu^*} (\mu^* - \mu(\theta_j)) E T_n(j).

algorithms.name: Rule phi* (sample-from-the-leader with upper confidence bounds g_ni)

conditions: rule satisfies R_n(theta) = o(n^a) for every a > 0 and every theta

source.quote: THEOREM 1. Assume that I(\theta, \lambda) satisfies (1.6) and (1.7), and that \Theta is such that ... (1.9). Let \varphi be a rule whose regret satisfies, for each fixed \theta = (\theta_1,...,\theta_k), the condition that as n \to \infty R_n(\theta) = o(n^a) for every a > 0 (1.10). Then for every \theta such that the \mu(\theta_j) are not all equal, \liminf R_n(\theta)/\log n \ge \sum_{j:\mu(\theta_j)<\mu^*} (\mu^* - \mu(\theta_j))/I(\theta_j, \theta^*).

results.notes: I(theta_j, theta*) is the KL divergence within the parametric family, mapped to KL_i. Text is OCR-garbled but the statement is standard.

conditions: arm j is suboptimal under theta

source.quote: THEOREM 2. Assume that I(\theta, \lambda) satisfies (1.6) and (1.7) and that \Theta satisfies (1.9). Fix j ... Let \varphi be any rule such that for every \theta \in \Theta_j^*, as n \to \infty \sum_{i\ne j} E_\theta T_n(i) = o(n^a) for every a > 0 ... Then for every \theta \in \Theta_j and every \epsilon > 0, ... and hence \liminf E_\theta T_n(j)/\log n \ge 1/I(\theta_j, \theta^*).

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm. Theorem also gives a high-probability statement (2.3) lim P(T_n(j) < (1-eps) log n / ((1+eps) I)) = 0, garbled in source; not recorded separately.

tuning: upper confidence bounds g_ni and estimates h_i satisfy (3.1)-(3.5)

source.quote: THEOREM 3. Assume that I(\theta, \lambda) satisfies (1.6) and (1.7) and that the functions g_ni and h_i satisfy (3.1)-(3.5). ... (i) For every \theta = (\theta_1,...,\theta_k) and every j such that \mu(\theta_j) < \mu(\theta^*), E_\theta T_n(j) \le (1/I(\theta_j,\theta^*) + o(1)) \log n.

results.notes: Pull-count bound. Section 4 constructs g_ni satisfying (3.1)-(3.5) for normal (known variance), Bernoulli, Poisson and double exponential families, so Theorem 3 applies to those.

tuning: upper confidence bounds g_ni and estimates h_i satisfy (3.1)-(3.5)

source.quote: (ii) Assume also that \theta satisfies (1.9). Then E_\theta T_n(j) \sim (\log n)/I(\theta_j, \theta^*) for every j such that \mu(\theta_j) < \mu(\theta^*), and the regret of \varphi^* satisfies (1.8).

results.notes: (1.8) is asymptotic equality, matching the Theorem 1 lower bound; recorded as limsup upper bound. Applies via Section 4 to Gaussian (known variance), Bernoulli, Poisson, double exponential.
